_about: Hand-written content of docs/unlocks.html (built by tools/pages/build_unlocks_page.py). One entry per game mechanic, shown at the Ascension it is unlocked at. Fields: name, asc (0-4), unlock (list of lines: how it is unlocked), sections (list of {title, text}; text may use blank lines for paragraphs).

sections.title: Abdication
sections.text: Abdication is the first reset introduced in the game. Stats counted in this Era are reset when you abdicate. Abdicating also converts the coins you made into Gems:

vars: the coins you made in this Reincarnation, all its Eras together
your total Gems after abdicating: the Gems you own plus the ones you gain

sections.title: Reincarnation
sections.text: Reincarnation is the second reset introduced in the game. Stats counted in this Reincarnation are reset when you reincarnate. To make the next Reincarnation you need to have a number of Gems that grows with every one you make:

vars: the Gems you need to have to make the n-th Reincarnation
the number of the Reincarnation you are making

sections.title: Ascension
sections.text: An Ascension is a special kind of Reincarnation that resets your economy and introduces new mechanics. Ascensions happen at Reincarnation 40, 100, 160 and 220. From Ascension 1 on, the Ascension penalty reduces the percentage bonuses of many upgrades, researches, spells and unique buildings. A bonus of v % becomes:

vars: the bonus before the penalty, in %
how many times the penalty is applied: your Ascension number minus the Ascension it starts at, plus 1 (usually just your Ascension number)

sections.after: Some effects are not reduced at all, and some are not reduced at Ascension 4. Further information about each Ascension and what it encompasses is given on its Unlocks page.

mechanics.name: Royal Exchanges
unlock: Available from the start (Reincarnation 0): the Royal Market opens as soon as you have chosen a faction.

card.name: Royal Market
card.text: Opens the Royal Market in the game, where you can purchase Royal Exchanges for Faction Coins. They can be bought multiple times for an increasing price per Faction Coin type.

sections.title: What they are
sections.text: Royal Exchanges are bought in the Royal Market with Faction Coins, one coin type per faction. Every exchange you buy adds to a bonus that multiplies all of your production. An exchange can be bought any number of times, and the price rises with every one you buy of the same coin type.

sections.title: Bonus per exchange
sections.text: The base bonus is 10% per exchange. This is the Individual Bonus shown in the Royal Market. Various things in the game affect it.

vars: additive increases to the Royal Exchange bonus
multiplicative increases to the Royal Exchange bonus, in %

sections.after: For example, Diplomacy (E30) and the Titan Set add to it, and Equivalence (A5875) and the Titan Lineage multiply it.

sections.title: Overall bonus
sections.text: The overall bonus multiplies your total production. With no exchanges bought it is 1. At Ascension 0 every exchange adds b% of your production: 100 exchanges at 10% give a multiplier of 11. From Ascension 1 the Ascension penalty below applies.

vars: the overall bonus, a multiplier on production
exchanges bought (Exchanges Made in the stats), all coin types together
1 at Ascension 0, see the Ascension penalty below

sections.after: For example, the Archon Heritage makes every exchange count for 10% more.

sections.title: Ascension penalty
sections.text: From Ascension 1 the overall bonus is raised to a power p that is below 1 instead of being used as it is. This is not the penalty of the researches (the A marks): the exchanges have their own formula, which weakens with every Ascension. The Individual Bonus shown in the Royal Market is not reduced, only the overall bonus is.

vars: increases to the Ascension multiplier from items

sections.after: For example, Hoarding (E1225) raises the Ascension multiplier.

sections.title: Cost
sections.text: The first exchange of a coin type costs 20 Faction Coins of that type. Each one you buy of that coin type makes the next one g times as expensive, so the price of the next one is about 20 · g to the power of the number already bought. Every coin type has its own count. The first formula gives the total price of buying k more when n are already bought; g is called the cost multiplier and starts at 1.1.

vars: exchanges of this coin type already bought

sections.after: For example, Intimidation (E1325) lowers the cost multiplier.

sections.title: What they are
sections.text: Spells are powers you cast with mana. Each spell has a mana cost, which is taken from your mana when you cast it, and most last for a limited time, during which their effect is active. A spell that is still active can't be cast again until it ends.

sections.title: What they are
sections.text: Buildings are bought with coins and produce coins every second. The price of each kind rises with every one you own.

link.text: All buildings, their production and cost

sections.title: What they are
sections.text: Factions are the peoples you can side with. Each faction has its own Faction Coins, unique buildings and upgrades. You start with the six vanilla factions, and more become available as you progress.

faction_notes.Dragon: Can be unlocked starting from Reincarnation 42

mechanics.name: Excavations
unlock: Available from the start (Reincarnation 0): buy the Archeology upgrade, which appears at 1e9 Gems and costs 1e29 coins. Then Excavation can be bought.

sections.title: What they are
sections.text: Excavations are bought with coins in the Excavation panel. Every excavation finds Faction Coins, and may find artifacts. The price of the next excavation rises with every one you make, until you reset your excavations. The excavations you made are kept when you Abdicate; a reset or a Reincarnation sets them back to zero.

sections.title: Cost
sections.text: Buying n excavations at once, when d have been made since your last reset, costs the sum of their prices. Each price is the cost multiplier r times the one before it, starting from a. From Ascension 1 the part of the multiplier above 1 is divided by 5A, so the price rises much more slowly.

vars: the coins the next n excavations cost
how many excavations you buy at once
the excavations made since your last Excavation Reset (your excavation depth)
the price of the first excavation after a reset
the cost multiplier before the Ascension is taken into account
the reductions of the excavation cost multiplier, below

lists.title: Examples of cost reduction multipliers:
items: Reality Crater, while Infinite Spiral is active

sections.title: Rubies
sections.text: You receive one Ruby each time you reach one of the depths below for the first time.

vars: the excavation depth that gives the k-th Ruby

sections.title: Excavation Resets
sections.text: A reset sets the excavations made since the last reset back to zero, so the price starts again at the first excavation. A regular reset costs Rubies, while free resets (from Ascension 1) cost nothing, but require you to meet a coin threshold based on your Reincarnation. Each free reset you make in a Reincarnation raises the amount needed for the next one, and it is counted in the stats as Excavation Resets (Free).

vars: the Rubies a regular reset costs
the excavations made since your last reset
the coins you need to have for a free reset (they are not spent)
the gems needed for your next Reincarnation
the free resets you have made in this Reincarnation

sections.after: The coin threshold for a free reset starts at 12 orders of magnitude below the number of coins needed to reach the gem requirement for the next Reincarnation, and goes up by 3 orders of magnitude with each free reset. See the Abdication section for the conversion formula.

sections.title: Faction Coins
sections.text: Every excavation finds Faction Coins. The amount is worked out for each excavation on its own, with d the excavations made since your last reset before this one, so it grows as you dig deeper and starts again after a reset.

vars: the Faction Coins one excavation finds
the excavations made since your last reset, before this one

mechanics.name: Challenges
unlock: Available from Reincarnation 2: the Challenges tab opens.

sections.title: What they are
sections.text: Challenges are trials that you must complete for each faction. A challenge entails one or two main tasks that you may have to actively build towards, along with a number of minor objectives to tick off. Completing a challenge grants various bonuses. A challenge completed for a faction does not necessarily help that faction.

lines.text: The Veteran Figurine lore artifact allows Mercenaries to benefit from all challenges.

mechanics.note: First unlocked at Reincarnation 2. More are unlocked as you advance through Reincarnations

mechanics.name: Researches
unlock: Available from Reincarnation 16 for the six vanilla factions, 24 for the Neutral factions, 32 for the Prestige factions and 75 for the Mercenaries.

sections.title: What they are
sections.text: Researches are upgrades that you unlock by investing coins and Faction Coins into a research branch. Doing so earns you Research Points in that branch, and more researches appear under it as you do. The Research Points you can invest are limited by your number of Reincarnations, and each branch only has room for a limited number of researches at a time.

mechanics.name: Legacies
unlock: Available from Ascension 4: the Legacy containers need Ascension 4.

sections.title: What they are
sections.text: Legacies let you use the upgrades of other factions. A Legacy is one tier (Bronze, Silver, Gold or Diamond) of a faction that is not part of your own line, which you choose in a Legacy container. Owning it makes that faction's upgrades of that tier available to you, in place of the treaty tier they would otherwise need. You cannot change your Legacies until you abdicate.

sections.title: Legacy containers
sections.text: You have four Legacy containers by default, and each one holds one Legacy. A Legacy costs coins, along with Faction Coins of the faction you take it from, and it costs more the further you are in the containers: the price depends on the number n of the container you choose it in, from 1 to 4. The Legacies of the prestige factions have a much higher base price than those of the other factions.

vars: the Sapphire Coins a Legacy costs
the number of the container (1 to 4, and 0 for the free container, which costs nothing)
the base price: $10^{39}$, or $10^{118}$ for a prestige faction
the Faction Coins a Legacy costs
the base amount: $10^{21}$, or $10^{45}$ for a prestige faction

sections.title: Legacy combos
sections.text: Legacy combos are bonus effects that need Legacies of two of the six base factions. There is one combo for each pair of them, 15 in total. You can have only one combo by default, and they reset when you abdicate. A combo costs 1e72 Sapphire Coins and 1e33 Faction Coins of each of its two factions. Click the object to see all of them.

mechanics.name: Bloodlines, Lineages and Sets
unlock: Bloodlines are available from Reincarnation 7, Lineages from Reincarnation 60 and Artifact Sets from Reincarnation 100.

sections.title: Bloodline
sections.text: Bloodlines are bonuses tied to a faction. Every faction except the Mercenaries has its own Bloodline. You can only have one Bloodline by default, it persists until you abdicate, and it does not suffer from Ascension penalties. Click the object to see all of them.

sections.title: Lineage
sections.text: Lineages are bonuses tied to a faction that grow with levels, and higher levels unlock perks. You can only have one Lineage, and it persists until you abdicate. It requires 400 Royal Exchanges and the Bloodline of a specific faction, and it cannot match any of your chosen factions. Click the object to see all of them, and click one to see its perks.

sections.title: Artifact Set
sections.text: Artifact Sets are bonuses that you unlock by finding the lore artifacts of a faction. You can only have one Set, and it persists until you abdicate. Most Sets give a second bonus once you also have their fourth artifact. Click the object to see all of them.

0.overview: Ascension 0 introduces a number of basic mechanics that stay relevant throughout the game. You start with the six vanilla factions, and you unlock the Neutral Factions, the Prestige Factions and the ability to do research. You also unlock the powerful Mercenary faction, which is only selectively available to you in later Ascensions.

sections.title: Excavations
sections.text: Excavations are unlocked by buying the Archeology upgrade. It appears in the Upgrades panel, under the Misc category, once you have 1e9 Gems, and it is only offered once: buying it gives you the Archeology Expedition trophy. After that you can make [Excavations](mechanics.html#excavations).

sections.title: Neutral Factions
sections.text: Each Neutral Faction is unlocked by buying its own upgrade. The upgrade appears once you have found two quest artifacts of the faction through [Excavations](mechanics.html#excavations) and meet the requirement they describe. The artifacts are found within a handful of excavations.

items: **Titan:** Ancient Stoneslab 1 and Ancient Stoneslab 2. Own 300 Halls of Legends to make Fragment of a Titan Statue available.
**Druid:** Fossilized Piece of Bark 1 and Fossilized Piece of Bark 2. Find 1,000,000 Faction Coins in the current Era to make Druidic Runestone available.
**Faceless:** Bone Fragment 1 and Bone Fragment 2. Play for 36 hours in total, over all your Eras and Reincarnations, to make Octopus Shaped Spine available.

sections.title: Prestige Factions
sections.text: The Prestige Factions (Dwarf and Drow) are unlocked in three steps. Unlike the Neutral Factions, they do not need any quest artifacts.

lists.title: **1. Passage to the Underworld.** This upgrade appears once you have made 200 excavations. Buying it starts the search of the Underworld and makes the two quests of the next step appear.

**2. The quests.** Sturdy Bearded Man's Quest (Dwarf) and Cloaked Shady Figure's Quest (Drow) are two upgrades that can only be bought while you meet their requirements. Buying one unlocks its faction.

**3. Underworld Diplomacy.** Until it is bought, the Dwarven and Drow Coins, Royal Exchanges and Heritages stay locked. It appears once you have unlocked the Dwarf or the Drow, but only below Reincarnation 3, and it has to be bought again after every Abdication and Reincarnation. From Reincarnation 3 on, these are unlocked without it.

sections.title: Challenges
sections.text: Challenges are unlocked at Reincarnation 2. You gain access immediately upon reaching Reincarnation 2, and you must buy the Challenge Power upgrade to benefit from them. More unlock as you advance through Reincarnations. See the [Challenges](challenges.html) page for all of them.

sections.title: Mercenaries
sections.text: The Mercenaries are unlocked in two steps.

lists.title: **1. Mercenary Tribute.** From Reincarnation 3 this upgrade becomes available, and its cost grows the longer you play in the Era. Buying it unlocks the Mercenary Oath trophy.
**2. Oath of the Mercenaries.** Once you own the Mercenary Oath trophy, this upgrade becomes available. Buying it allows you to ally with the Mercenaries.

sections.after: From Reincarnation 3 the Dwarven and Drow Coins, Royal Exchanges and Heritages are also available, without needing to buy Underworld Diplomacy.

sections.title: Bloodlines
sections.text: Bloodlines are available immediately as soon as you reach Reincarnation 7. See [Bloodlines](mechanics.html#bloodline) on the Mechanics page.

sections.title: Spiritual Surge
sections.text: Spiritual Surge, a spell whose power is based on your Reincarnations, is unlocked immediately upon reaching Reincarnation 14. See the [Spells](spells.html#spiritual-surge) page.

sections.title: Vanilla Faction Research
sections.text: Researches are unlocked for the vanilla factions by purchasing their unique building and at least one research facility, which becomes available to purchase once you own your unique building. The unique buildings each have an associated unlock quest that you must complete once. Each research facility unlocks a branch in the research page and must only be bought once. Each facility is made available to one of the six vanilla factions. Prestige Factions cannot perform research yet, so allying with them will revoke your ability to buy your unique building, and thus access to research. See the [Research](research.html) page.

sections.title: Neutral Faction Research
sections.text: Research becomes available for the Neutral Factions (Titan, Druid and Faceless). Their first Unique Buildings (Olympian Hall, Stonehenge and Sunken City) are unlocked too, along with the Key to the Lost City artifact.

sections.title: Prestige Faction Research
sections.text: Research becomes available for the Prestige Factions (Dwarf and Drow). Their Unique Buildings (Dwarven Forge and Spider Sanctuary) are unlocked too, along with the Earth Core artifact.
